title: Introduce tolerant-strict response_format with stream snapshotting and toolcall safeguards
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers expect deterministic structured output but streaming and tool/function-calls make strict JSON enforcement brittle. Motivation: Provide a compromise mode that preserves developer ergonomics for OpenAI-compatible clients while giving operators observability and recoverability for streaming truncation and schema violations. This PR adds a new response_format mode called 'tolerant-strict' that enforces JSON Schema validation at completion but accepts and records partial/ambiguous stream tokens, emits structured error metadata, and exposes a small resume snapshot token that downstream callers (SDKs or gateway) can use to request a resumed/repair call. Design summary: 1) response_format=tolerant-strict: at the start of the response stream the runtime emits a single metadata event (X-JSON-Mode: tolerant-strict) and includes a small opaque resume token when partial deserialization is observed. 2) Stream snapshotting: on schema parse failures or token-level truncation we capture a compact snapshot of the last valid JSON prefix and the syntactic error location; this snapshot is encoded into the resume token (HMACed) and stored for short TTL in the control-plane cache. 3) Toolcall safety: tool/function call invocation during tolerant-strict mode is gated behind a 'toolcall_fence' that verifies tool arguments against the schema before executing and returns a clear error_code + remediation_hint when an invocation would be unsafe. 4) OpenAI compat: runtime maintains the same top-level streaming frames (data/error) but extends the error frame with an openai_compat.metadata object (error_code, resume_token, partial_json) for non-breaking clients. Implementation notes: - Runtime: additions to the streaming dispatcher and response validator (validate_stream.cc) implement checkpointing and token anchoring. - Control plane: resume token store implemented as a short-lived KV with encrypted payload and rate-limited retrieval. - SDKs: lightweight helpers added to Python/TS SDKs to transparently exchange resume tokens and attempt auto-repair calls when enabled. - Telemetry: new metrics (schema.validation.attempts, schema.validation.failures, resume.token.generated, resume.token.used) and a tracing span (response.schema.repair) are emitted. Backwards compatibility: Default behavior remains unchanged; tolerant-strict must be explicitly requested by clients. Rollout: feature-flag gated on Canary -> Regional -> Global with a migration window and automatic disabling if resume failures exceed thresholds. Testing: unit + integration tests added, plus end-to-end smoke run against openai-compat test harness. See checklist/comments for details.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add tolerant-strict constants and basic dispatcher hooks; 2) implement stream snapshot encoder + resume token store; 3) SDK helpers and tests + docs updates (CHANGELOG snippet)
changed_files: runtime/streaming/validate_stream.cc, runtime/streaming/stream_dispatcher.cc, controlplane/resume_store/kv_store.cc, sdk/python/redwood/response_helpers.py, sdk/ts/src/responseHelpers.ts, docs/api/response_format.md, docs/ops/rollout-playbook.md, tests/integration/tolerant_strict_e2e.test, CHANGELOG.md
review_comments: Rajan Patel: Important feature, but two concerns: 1) resume token size needs an upper bound so we don't accidentally bloat streaming frames. 2) Can we avoid storing partial_json in the token for PII-sensitive requests?
Maya Chen (reply): token capped at 1KB and we store only a hashed prefix + minimal syntactic context. We added a config to opt-out of partial_json capture for KMS-protected customers.
Elena Torres: Please add a unit test that simulates interleaved toolcalls with tolerant-strict to ensure toolcall_fence prevents side effects on malformed args.
Maya Chen (reply): added tests in tests/integration/tolerant_strict_e2e.test and a focused unit test in runtime/streaming/validate_stream_test.cc
Liam O'Connor: CI flaked once on the new tracing span; ensure traces are no-op when tracing disabled.
Maya Chen (reply): guard added so tracing spans are created only when tracing.enabled=true; re-ran CI
ci_log: Initial CI: failed (flaky span test) -> added guard -> rerun -> pass (all checks green). Coverage: +0.9% on streaming package. Lint: clean.
release_notes: Added response_format=tolerant-strict: validates JSON schema at completion while providing resume tokens and structured error metadata for streaming and tool/function-call scenarios. SDKs updated with helpers to consume resume tokens. Feature is opt-in and feature-flag gated.
notes_for_ops: Canary rollout steps in docs/ops/rollout-playbook.md; watch metrics schema.validation.failures and resume.token.used. Default disable threshold: 1% failure rate over 5m window.
qa_summary: Added unit tests covering token generation, token expiry, toolcall_fence behavior, and end-to-end integration against openai-compat harness. Local fuzzer found two edge-cases which were patched (unterminated arrays and multi-tool interleaving).
security_considerations: Resume token payloads are HMACed and encrypted in control-plane store; partial_json capture is opt-out for customers with PII controls. Audit logs record resume token creation and retrieval events.
manual_steps: 1) Enable feature-flag 'response_format.tolerant_strict' in Canary org. 2) Deploy control-plane KV migration with encryption keys. 3) Monitor telemetry and revert via feature-flag if failures cross threshold.
author_pr_comments: This PR is intentionally conservative about capturing user content; operators can opt-out via config. SDKs include opt-in auto-repair stacks to keep app-level behavior explicit.
acknowledgements: Design consults with Platform team (Rajan) and Security (Elena). Thanks to the SDK leads for coordination.
changelog_entry: feat(api): response_format=tolerant-strict for resumable schema validation and safer toolcalls (Maya Chen)
